title: Minimum Operations to Make Array Modulo Alternating I
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, determine the least number of operations needed to adjust each element by +1 or -1 so that the array becomes modulo alternating.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, determine the least number of operations needed to adjust each element by +1 or -1 so that the array becomes modulo alternating. A modulo alternating array has two distinct integers x and y (0 <= x, y < k) where for even indices, nums[i] % k equals x, and for odd indices, nums[i] % k equals y.
constraints: One operation changes one value by one in either direction; residues wrap modulo k.
Choose distinct even- and odd-index residues and minimize operations.
hints: Only residues matter, and there are k choices for each parity.
Enumerate distinct target residues and add circular distance for every element.
Use min(abs difference, k-abs difference), retaining the cheapest pair.
Each unit edit moves one step around the residue cycle, so circular distance is exact.
editorial: Each unit edit moves one step around the residue cycle, so circular distance is exact.
